question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: NAME. name must match the NAME grammar, else -> throws, before text is read at all. This includes the empty text, a lowercase name, "SIG:", a name with a space, a dot or a trailing line break, and non-ASCII letters. The name "CITED" (the attribute-only keyword, which never starts a directive, R6) also -> throws, whatever text holds.

LINES. text is cut into physical lines at each CARRIAGE RETURN + LINE FEED pair (one break), each lone CARRIAGE RETURN and each lone LINE FEED. LINE SEPARATOR, PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR and NEXT LINE do NOT break a line. Each line then loses every BYTE ORDER MARK inside its LEAD — the longest leading run of SEP characters and BYTE ORDER MARKs, in any mix (the SEP characters stay, in order) — and after that every SEP character at its very end. One pass reaches the fixed point: BOM SPACE BOM "x" becomes SPACE "x" (so an unindented line can become indented). A mark after the first character outside the LEAD is content. CITED FIDELITY package

SKIPPED lines. A line left empty by R2 is skipped (a line of NO-BREAK SPACE, LINE TABULATION or any other non-SEP character is NOT empty). Otherwise its INDENT is its leading run of SEP characters (possibly empty) and its CONTENT is the rest. A line whose CONTENT starts with "#" is a comment and is skipped. Skipped lines never end a directive: lines after them still continue it.

QUOTED SPANS. CONTENT is scanned left to right for quoted spans. A QUOTATION MARK OPENS a span only at a token start: it is the first character of CONTENT, or the character before it is in the OPENER set, or it is the character directly after the closing mark of the span just closed (two literals back to back). From the opener the span runs to and including the next QUOTATION MARK that is not the partner of an escape pair, where an escape pair is a REVERSE SOLIDUS plus the ONE character after it, whatever that character is (QUOTATION MARK, REVERSE SOLIDUS, LINE SEPARATOR or an astral character alike). The scan resumes after the closing mark. When CONTENT ends first (no closing mark, or a REVERSE SOLIDUS last), that opener protects nothing and no later span exists on the line. Any other QUOTATION MARK — an inch mark after a digit, one after a letter, a SOLIDUS, "*", "+" or "?", a closing parenthesis or bracket, a QUOTATION MARK that closed no span, a NO-BREAK SPACE or a byte-order mark — opens nothing; a closing mark need not end a token. CITED FIDELITY package

COMMENT CUT. On every non-skipped line, CONTENT is cut at the FIRST "#" that has a SEP character immediately before it, a SEP character or the end of CONTENT immediately after it, and does not lie strictly inside a quoted span (R4): that "#", the SEP run immediately before it and everything after it are dropped. The result is CODE. "a#b", "a #b", a "#" next to a NO-BREAK SPACE or IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, and a "#" inside a quoted span are not cuts.

DIRECTIVE LINE. A line with an empty INDENT is examined as a candidate directive: its NAME-WORD is CODE up to (not including) the first SEP character, or all of CODE when there is none; REST is CODE from that SEP character on (it keeps its leading separator), or the empty text when there is none. A NAME-WORD that is a NAME followed by exactly one ":" is read as that NAME ("SIG: x" is SIG, "SIG:: x" is not). When the NAME-WORD (so read) matches the NAME grammar and is not the attribute keyword "CITED", the line STARTS a new directive with that name — whether or not the name is a known directive; "EARNED" and "ANCHOR" do start directives — and its first piece is ATTR-CUT(REST). Any other character after the name ("SIGNAL", "SIG-X", NO-BREAK SPACE, IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, LINE SEPARATOR) makes it a different NAME-WORD: "ORACLE" never matches an "ORACLE-CLASS" line, and a name glued to its arguments by non-SEP whitespace or by an invisible format character (ZERO WIDTH SPACE, WORD JOINER, MONGOLIAN VOWEL SEPARATOR) is not a directive; nor is "NAME:" glued that way, nor a line whose CONTENT starts with such a character before a name (the parser reports these; the value ignores the report).

CONTINUATION. Every other non-skipped line — an indented line, or an unindented line whose NAME-WORD fails R6 (prose, lowercase words, a line beginning with NO-BREAK SPACE, a column-0 "CITED" or "CITED:" line) — continues the most recent directive started above it, contributing the piece ATTR-CUT(SPACE + CODE). Before any directive has started such a line is ignored.

ATTR-CUT(s). An ATTRIBUTE KEYWORD is one of the words CITED/EARNED/ANCHOR occurring as a whole token: preceded by one or more SEP characters, followed by a SEP character or the end of s, and not lying inside a quoted span of the line's CONTENT (R4), where it is data. ATTR-CUT keeps the part of s before the first such run-and-keyword, with leading and trailing SEP characters removed; with no keyword it is s with leading and trailing SEP characters removed. Since both a directive line's REST and a continuation's piece begin with a separator, a keyword FIRST on either kind of line yields the empty piece; a keyword glued to other letters, or followed by any non-SEP character (":" or ","), is content.

RESULT. The first directive in text order whose name equals name (exactly, case-sensitively) decides: its pieces (first the directive line's, then each continuation's, in order) are filtered to the NON-EMPTY ones and joined with one SPACE between neighbours; nothing else is trimmed. No non-empty piece -> "" (the empty text). No directive named name -> none. Later directives of the same name never count.
